query: Orrery, a small independent planetarium and night-sky shop in Bristol's harbourside. 60-seat dome, live presenter-led shows, school sessions on weekdays, rooftop telescope evenings on clear Friday nights, shop selling star maps, telescopes and kits. Landing page with shows, booking, shop, membership, telescope nights, testimonials, FAQ.

matched_industry.name: E-Commerce & Product Catalogs
matched_industry.layout_archetype: Merchandising Hero + High-Scannability Filterable Product Grid
matched_industry.first_viewport_priority: Hero product imagery, clear price/availability cues, fast category navigation

palette.notes: Neutral daylight backdrop that never distorts product photography colors

matched_industry.motion_language: Quick 180ms image hover zoom, tactile cart drawer slide-over, zero layout shift (CLS = 0)
anti_patterns: Blocking newsletter popups on initial load

category_cliches: White grid of identical product cards with a pill 'Add to cart'
distinctiveness.instruction: Subject first: list the objects, tools and moments a visitor actually sees in this business (a bakery: loaves, the oven, flour; an optician: frames, lenses, the test chart). The first screen must show the most characteristic of them as authored art at scale, so a stranger can name the business with the text covered. Then write down 3 concrete references from the brand's own world (local architecture, craft traditions, signage, landscape, the material itself) and derive palette, pattern, and type voice from them. Place: Bristol's — what does it look like there, specifically? The clichés below are generic *treatments* (layouts, kits, palettes), not the subject's own objects: avoid the treatments, never the subject.

matched_styles.name: Atelier Tactile Minimalism
characteristics: Warm paper and limestone neutrals (`#FAF8F5`) rather than sterile `#FFFFFF`
Unhurried vertical rhythm (`96px–140px` section spacing) and monograph captions
Zero decorative card wrappers; imagery and typography sit directly on the canvas

matched_styles.name: Crisp Product Workbench
characteristics: Interactive live product state demonstrations in the hero instead of static screenshots
Subtle surface layering (`#FCFCFA` -> `#F2F3EE`) with crisp 1px borders
Clear scannable feature proof and transparent pricing architecture

directions.title: Direction A — E-Commerce & Product Catalogs (Editorial & Structural Clarity)
directions.layout_composition: Merchandising Hero + High-Scannability Filterable Product Grid on an exposed structural grid where type and the subject's object share one asymmetric 7:5 composition, generous section rhythm (clamp(5.5rem, 9vw, 9rem)), and each section shaped by its content
directions.visual_identity: Type as image: display set large enough to become architecture, ruled structure drawn from the subject's own notation (charts, labels, tickets), no floating card clutter

palette.notes: Neutral daylight backdrop that never distorts product photography colors

directions.content_treatment: Lead with the subject's most characteristic object at scale and the real action (buy, book) working in the first viewport; specifics as scannable tables, never big-number stat blocks
directions.motion_choreography: Decide per content: a typographic load sequence, content-shaped section entrances, crisp 160-240ms ease-out interactions; reduced-motion keeps fades only

directions.title: Direction B — E-Commerce & Product Catalogs (Kinetic Narrative & Choreographed Stage)
directions.layout_composition: Full-bleed choreographed stage with pinned ScrollTrigger narrative sequence, staggered asymmetric showcase, and magnetic CTA rail
directions.visual_identity: High-drama contrast stage with expressive display typography, tactile depth planes, and bespoke SVG/3D focal points

palette.notes: Saturated cobalt colour field with sun-yellow and mint

directions.content_treatment: Story-driven sequential progression: Problem tension -> Interactive live artifact -> Quantified proof
directions.motion_choreography: GSAP timeline entrance + ScrollTrigger pinned sequence + pointer parallax with `gsap.matchMedia()` reduced-motion guard

directions.title: Direction C — E-Commerce & Product Catalogs (Tactile Product Workbench & Interactive Proof)
directions.layout_composition: Interactive hero where the visitor operates the subject itself (try a frame, fit a part, set a date) immediately above the fold, then sections built from real product structure
directions.visual_identity: Tactile, rebuilt controls in the world's own material (dials, tickets, swatches), one depth strategy, every atom (buttons, inputs, focus) redrawn in that vocabulary

palette.notes: Sage daylight with graphite text and rust accents

directions.content_treatment: Interactive proof-first: let the user manipulate live tabs, filters, or calculators right inside the hero
directions.motion_choreography: State-driven spring transitions (180ms–280ms) and FLIP layout morphs on user interaction

workflow_guidance: Mode A (New Website): the user's prompt wins over everything here. The 3 directions are structural raw material (layout, content treatment, dials), not finished looks; the visual world comes from art direction.

DISTINCTIVENESS: Read `distinctiveness` first. If `match_confidence` is `none` or `weak`, the industry profile is only a fallback; build the visual world from the brief's place and material cues instead, and do not ship any listed category cliché unless the brief asks for it.

ART DIRECTION (load `skills/layoza-art-direction`): commit to ONE specific world. Derive the world from far (place, notation, print traditions), keep the subject up close (the trade's object as the signature interaction, at scale), rule out the category reflex and its obvious opposite, and put the visitor's real action in the first viewport. Let colour own whole sections. Decide motion and tools per design; nothing is mandatory.

ENGINEERING LESSONS: sticky headers need `html { scroll-padding-top: <header height + 1rem> }` (WCAG 2.4.11); web fonts need metric-adjusted fallback `@font-face` (size-adjust / ascent-override) or the font swap re-wraps headings and fails CLS; scroll reveals must end visible.
TYPE & LEADING: Keep multi-line display headings at `line-height >= 1.0` so ascenders and descenders never collide.

LAYOUT SAFETY: Keep short header links/buttons on one line (`white-space: nowrap`), give side-by-side heading columns >= 16px of clear space, collapse multi-column grids before gaps exceed the viewport, and size any <canvas> from a fixed-size container with devicePixelRatio capped at 2.
Verify in a real browser with `layoza qa <file-or-url>` (1440/768/375): it measures contrast, overflow, clipping, nav, scroll reveals, and lab Core Web Vitals; fix every error.
